objective: Theory, proof attempt and exact checks. Restate the closure behind creation as a tetrahedron rule. Compare creation with and without a receiving side (a knot space split at a point, standing in for a line) on census, plane and composite near sides, in the strong form: new knots off the side, and new knots through it. Classify one- and two-point hidden gadgets by whether they keep creation, to locate what an intact side must not encode. Prove what can be proved: the half in which the side removes no creation, and the pendant-line case; isolate the rest as a precise statement.
status: Proved by TWO-BIT-SCREEN-20261105-001A-P001: the elimination closure behind creation is a tetrahedron rule; an intact Fano side attached at a line never removes creation (the new knots off it are the closed space's, generated knots through it have generated port shadows, and no crossing knot meets two hidden classes), and the same holds for a pendant line; that the side never adds creation reduces to the pendant-line statement (one new point on one new line never adds creation; 117,344 cases, open); a point on two or three new lines can create (8 of 27 profiles), and every knot-space side tried has only subcube points
title: Hidden points and the two-bit screening lemma
